findings.claim: Chest pain presents cardiac distress, presumed to contraindicate other transport
findings.quote: Exhibits signs and symptoms of acute respiratory distress or cardiac distress such as shortness of breath or chest pain
findings.case_fact: The ambulance report states that the beneficiary was being transported due to chest pain.

findings.claim: Emergency treatment was given during transport
findings.quote: Required oxygen or other emergency treatment during transport to the nearest appropriate facility
findings.case_fact: The ambulance report indicates that the beneficiary received emergency services during the ambulance transport.

findings.claim: Multiple therapy disciplines (PT and OT) were provided
findings.quote: required the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines
findings.case_fact: Occupational therapy was provided almost every day for periods of time totaling between 15 and 120 minutes per day.

findings.claim: Intensive therapy of about 3 hours daily was asserted
findings.quote: at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week
findings.case_fact: the patient received three hours daily of therapy services

findings.claim: Measurable improvement was achieved
findings.quote: make measurable improvement
findings.case_fact: I.W. had succeeded in raising all her ADL levels, most of them to her goal level

findings.claim: Oral medications by a nurse are generally not skilled care; patient took pill medications
findings.quote: The administration of oral medications by a nurse is not reasonable and necessary skilled nursing care
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was taking a variety of medications in pill form

findings.claim: Prefilling insulin syringes is not skilled; a caregiver gave insulin
findings.quote: The prefilling of syringes with insulin (or other medication that is self-injected) does not require the skills of a licensed nurse
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary had a caregiver who provided assistance with activities of daily living as well as the administration of oral medications and injections of insulin

findings.claim: Dosage was being adjusted so prothrombin monitoring is reasonable and necessary
findings.quote: Where the documentation shows that the dosage is being adjusted, monitoring would be reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: his physician modified the Coumadin dosages twice

findings.claim: Skilled observation needed until condition stabilizes
findings.quote: until the clinical condition and/or patient's treatment regimen has stabilized
findings.case_fact: Pursuant to the plan of care, the nurses also did regular cardiovascular and pulmonary checks

findings.claim: Passages give no clear necessity criteria for ground transport; BLS definition requires medically necessary services, none shown
findings.quote: the provision of medically necessary supplies and services
findings.case_fact: Nothing in the record reflects that the beneficiary required or was provided pain medications, oxygen, or any treatment during the evaluation or ambulance trip.

findings.claim: Air transport requires that ground ambulance was not appropriate; appellant conceded ground was reasonable
findings.quote: The beneficiary’s medical condition required immediate and rapid ambulance transportation that could not have been provided by ground ambulance
findings.case_fact: the appellant concedes that “ground transportation to a closer hospital was reasonable” in this case.

findings.claim: Stable vitals weigh against need for air transport
findings.quote: approve claims only if the beneficiary’s medical condition is such that transportation by either basic or advanced life support ground ambulance is not appropriate
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s vital signs were stable at the time of transfer

findings.claim: Hospital-to-hospital transfer requires sending hospital lacking adequate facilities; sending hospital had trauma center
findings.quote: the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient
findings.case_fact: It was determined that the sending hospital also has a trauma center.

findings.claim: Documentation did not identify the unavailable service
findings.quote: Examples of such specialized medical services that are generally not available at all type of facilities
findings.case_fact: The documentation did not state what specific service was not available at the first hospital.

findings.claim: Oxygen requirement meets presumption of emergency treatment during transport
findings.quote: Required oxygen or other emergency treatment during transport to the nearest appropriate facility
findings.case_fact: The Physician Certification Statement (PCS) signed by the registered nurse on the date of ambulance transportation states that the beneficiary also required oxygen.

findings.claim: Recent pacemaker surgery and monitoring need support ambulance
findings.quote: The patient was suffering
findings.case_fact: it was “absolutely necessary” to take him from the hospital to the rehabilitation center by ambulance with a cardiac monitor

findings.claim: Multiple therapy disciplines were planned
findings.quote: required the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines
findings.case_fact: providing daily occupational and physical therapy

findings.claim: Measurable improvement was shown
findings.quote: make measurable improvement
findings.case_fact: had moved from total assist for walking to modified independence in walking

findings.claim: Passages address admission orders, not whether inpatient status was necessary here
findings.quote: the ordering practitioner approves and accepts responsibility for the admission decision
findings.case_fact: Decision to change from observation to inpt status was made in ERROR.

findings.claim: Ambulance to a physician-directed clinic is not covered; facility was an urgent care clinic staffed by a physician
findings.quote: Ambulance service to a physician’s office or a physician-directed clinic is not covered.
findings.case_fact: is staffed by a physician “during day hours only, and is considered an urgent care facility.”

findings.claim: Adult day care absences do not defeat homebound status
findings.quote: regular absences for the purpose of participating in therapeutic, psychosocial, or medical treatment in an adult day-care program
findings.case_fact: absences from the home, though infrequent, included adult day care and doctor visits.

findings.claim: Infrequent absences are compatible with homebound
findings.quote: the absences from the home are infrequent
findings.case_fact: The re-certification further noted that the beneficiary was unable to leave the home without taxing efforts.

findings.claim: Skilled observation justified while regimen unstable
findings.quote: until the clinical condition and/or patient's treatment regimen has stabilized
findings.case_fact: immediately prior to the dates of service the beneficiary’s condition necessitated medication changes

findings.claim: Passages cover admission order/certification and non-covered services, not inpatient necessity for chest pain
findings.quote: The admission order is evidence of the decision by the ordering practitioner to admit the beneficiary to inpatient status.
findings.case_fact: He was initially placed in observation status but subsequently admitted to inpatient status.

findings.claim: Transfer covered only to nearest appropriate hospital; nearest was 133 miles vs 203 billed
findings.quote: is covered only if the hospital to which the patient is transferred is the nearest one with appropriate facilities
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was not taken to the nearest medically-appropriate facility, which would have been a distance of only 133 miles from the transferring facility.

findings.claim: Cardiology need at sending hospital is recognized
findings.quote: the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient
findings.case_fact: The transfer occurred so that the beneficiary would be treated in a hospital where specialist cardiologist services were available.

findings.claim: Skilled SLP services are covered where only an SLP can provide them and improvement or maintenance is expected
findings.quote: Speech-language pathology would be covered where a skilled service can only be provided by a speech-language pathologist
findings.case_fact: dysphagia therapy was ordered twice a week for 8 weeks in the care plan signed by the physician

findings.claim: Coverage does not depend solely on improvement potential
findings.quote: Coverage of speech-language pathology services is not determined solely on the presence or absence of a beneficiary’s potential for improvement
findings.case_fact: The therapy notes of the second four week period record “steady improvements,”

findings.claim: Observation not necessary where signs are longstanding and no treatment change
findings.quote: observation and assessment by a nurse is not reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the illness or injury
findings.case_fact: the QIC noted that there had been no changes in the beneficiary’s medications or plan of care

findings.claim: Record must document rationale for continued skilled observation
findings.quote: Information from the patient's home health record must document the rationale that demonstrates that there is a reasonable potential for a future complication
findings.case_fact: the record did not indicate that the home health agency had thoroughly assessed the cause of the palpitations.

findings.claim: Adult day care attendance does not by itself defeat homebound status
findings.quote: recognizes that they ordinarily furnish psychosocial services
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary leaves home four days every week to engage in “sheltered workshop” activities

findings.claim: Hours are within part-time limits
findings.quote: less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week
findings.case_fact: about seven hours of home health nursing and aide assistance per week is needed

findings.claim: Skilled nurse visits to pour a pillbox and oversee aides are not necessary skilled care
findings.quote: skilled nursing care would not be considered reasonable and necessary to treat the illness or injury
findings.case_fact: a skilled nurse visited the beneficiary approximately once every two weeks to fill a mediplanner with pills and oversee home health aides.

findings.claim: No documented reasonable potential for change
findings.quote: Information from the patient's home health record must document the rationale that demonstrates that there is a reasonable potential for a future complication
findings.case_fact: The plans of care do not contain physician’s orders for observation and assessment

findings.claim: Passages address non-covered services, not inpatient necessity for hernia repair
findings.quote: Medical and hospital services are sometimes required to treat a condition that arises as a result of services that are not covered
findings.case_fact: that occurred as a result of a sigmoid colon resection with colostomy in 2003

findings.claim: Wound care is skilled nursing when a nurse is needed
findings.quote: is considered to be a skilled nursing service
findings.case_fact: provided wound care, including cleansing and dressing the wound

findings.claim: Diabetes can adversely affect healing
findings.quote: has a reasonable potential to adversely affect healing (e.g., diabetes)
findings.case_fact: a principal diagnosis of type II diabetes, uncomplicated.

findings.claim: Services family or unskilled caregivers can perform are not covered skilled care
findings.quote: including when the services needed do not require skilled nursing care because they could safely and effectively be performed by the patient or unskilled caregivers
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary's family administered her medications without problems

findings.claim: Skilled care must be required; diabetes was controlled orally
findings.quote: so long as the beneficiary requires skilled care for the services to be safely and effectively provided
findings.case_fact: nurses notes reflect that the beneficiary was not symptomatic and received an oral diabetic agent, rather than injections.

findings.claim: Gait training is reasonable and necessary if it can improve walking
findings.quote: considered reasonable and necessary if they can be expected to materially improve or maintain the patient's ability to walk
findings.case_fact: diagnoses of degenerative joint disease of the right shoulder and arthritis of the lower extremities.

findings.claim: Skilled gait training occurred with improvement
findings.quote: The patient’s response to therapy must be documented.
findings.case_fact: Upon discharge, this score had improved to 18/28, signifying a moderate fall risk.
